content: Lopinavir and ritonavir should not be administered once daily in children or adolescents; instead, they should be given every 12 hours. The safety and efficacy of these drugs in children under 2 weeks of age have not been established. Lopinavir and ritonavir increase the levels or effects of alfuzosin by inhibiting the metabolism mediated by the hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4. This combination is contraindicated. Lopinavir increases the levels or effects of amiodarone by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism, while amiodarone increases ritonavir levels via P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Ritonavir also increases amiodarone levels by reducing its metabolism. This combination is contraindicated. Lopinavir increases the levels or effects of astemizole by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. This combination is contraindicated. Cobicistat increases ritonavir levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. This combination is contraindicated. Lopinavir increases the levels or effects of bromocriptine by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. This combination is contraindicated. Lopinavir increases the levels or effects of budesonide by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. This combination is contraindicated. Lopinavir and ritonavir increase the levels or effects of cobimetinib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. This combination is contraindicated. Ritonavir increases the levels or effects of conivaptan by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Lopinavir has the same effect. Co-administration of conivaptan with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors is contraindicated. Lopinavir and ritonavir increase the levels or effects of dihydroergotamine (including intranasal formulations) by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. This combination is contraindicated. Disulfiram increases the toxicity of ritonavir by inhibiting aldehyde dehydrogenase. This interaction is associated only with the oral solution of ritonavir, which contains 42% alcohol. This combination is contraindicated. Lopinavir increases the levels of elbasvir/grazoprevir through other mechanisms, potentially increasing the risk of ALT elevations due to significant increases in grazoprevir plasma concentrations. This combination is contraindicated. Ritonavir increases the levels or effects of elagolix through other mechanisms. Concomitant use of elagolix with strong OATP1B1 inhibitors is contraindicated. Lopinavir increases the levels or effects of eletriptan by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. This combination is contraindicated. Ritonavir increases the levels or effects of eliglustat by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Strong CYP3A4 inhibitors are contraindicated in poor or intermediate metabolizers of eliglustat. In extensive metabolizers, the eliglustat dose should be reduced from 84 mg twice daily to 84 mg once daily. Eliglustat is contraindicated if strong or moderate CYP2D6 inhibitors are co-administered with strong or moderate CYP3A inhibitors. Ritonavir increases the levels or effects of elvitegravir/cobicistat/emtricitabine/tenofovir DF by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. This combination is contraindicated because elvitegravir/cobicistat/emtricitabine/tenofovir DF is a complete regimen for HIV and should not be administered with other antiretrovirals. Enzalutamide decreases the levels or effects of ritonavir and lopinavir by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Ritonavir increases enzalutamide levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. This combination is contraindicated. Lopinavir increases the levels or effects of eplerenone by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. This combination is contraindicated. Ritonavir and lopinavir increase the levels or effects of ergoloid mesylates and ergonovine by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. These combinations are contraindicated. Ritonavir and lopinavir increase the levels or effects of finerenone by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. This combination is contraindicated. Ritonavir and lopinavir increase the levels or effects of flibanserin by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration of flibanserin with moderate or strong CYP3A4 inhibitors is contraindicated due to the risk of severe hypotension or syncope. Lopinavir and ritonavir increase the levels or effects of gepirone by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. This combination is contraindicated. Goserelin increases the toxicity of lopinavir by prolonging the QTc interval, increasing the risk of torsades de pointes. This combination is contraindicated. Ritonavir and lopinavir increase the levels or effects of irinotecan (including liposomal formulations) by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism or P-glycoprotein efflux transporter. These combinations are contraindicated. Lopinavir increases the levels or effects of isavuconazonium sulfate by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. This combination is contraindicated. Ritonavir and lopinavir increase the levels or effects of ivabradine by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration of ivabradine with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors is contraindicated. Lefamulin increases lopinavir levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. This combination is contraindicated due to the risk of QT interval prolongation. Leuprolide increases the toxicity of lopinavir by prolonging the QTc interval, increasing the risk of torsades de pointes. This combination is contraindicated. Lopinavir and ritonavir increase the levels of lomitapide by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. This combination is contraindicated due to the risk of significantly increased lomitapide levels. Ritonavir and lopinavir increase the levels or effects of lonafarnib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration with strong or moderate CYP3A4 inhibitors is contraindicated. Ritonavir and lopinavir increase the levels or effects of lovastatin by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. This combination is contraindicated due to the risk of myopathy, including rhabdomyolysis. Ritonavir increases the levels or effects of lurasidone by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration of lurasidone with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors is contraindicated. Lopinavir increases the levels or effects of mavacamten by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. This combination is contraindicated due to the risk of heart failure from systolic dysfunction. Ritonavir increases the levels or effects of mavorixafor by inhibiting CYP2D6 metabolism. This combination is contraindicated. Ritonavir and lopinavir increase the levels or effects of methylergonovine by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. This combination is contraindicated. Ritonavir and lopinavir increase the levels or effects of naloxegol by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors is contraindicated due to the risk of opioid withdrawal symptoms. Lopinavir increases the levels or effects of pacritinib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. This combination is contraindicated. Ritonavir increases the levels of pimozide by decreasing its metabolism, leading to a risk of QT interval prolongation. This combination is contraindicated. Lopinavir increases the levels of pitavastatin by decreasing its metabolism. This combination is contraindicated. Ritonavir and lopinavir increase the levels of regorafenib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. This combination is contraindicated. Lopinavir and ritonavir increase the levels of salmeterol by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. This combination is contraindicated due to the potential for increased toxicity. Lopinavir and ritonavir increase the levels of simvastatin by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. This combination is contraindicated due to the risk of myopathy, including rhabdomyolysis. St. John’s Wort decreases the levels or effects of ritonavir by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. This combination is contraindicated. Lopinavir increases the levels of tinidazole by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Tinidazole increases the toxicity of lopinavir and ritonavir by inhibiting aldehyde dehydrogenase. These interactions are associated only with the oral solution of ritonavir, which contains 42% alcohol. These combinations are contraindicated. Tipranavir increases lopinavir levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. This combination is contraindicated. Lopinavir increases the levels of triazolam by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. This combination is contraindicated. Lopinavir increases the levels of ubrogepant by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. This combination is contraindicated. Ritonavir increases the levels of venetoclax by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors is contraindicated during the initial ramp-up dosing phase of venetoclax. Ritonavir and lopinavir increase the levels of voclosporin by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. This combination is contraindicated. Voriconazole increases ritonavir levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism, while ritonavir decreases voriconazole levels by increasing its metabolism. This combination is contraindicated. Ritonavir and lopinavir increase the levels of acalabrutinib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors should be avoided. Ritonavir and lopinavir increase the levels of adagrasib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors should be avoided until adagrasib concentrations reach steady-state. Ritonavir and lopinavir increase the levels of ado-trastuzumab emtansine by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors should be avoided. Ritonavir and lopinavir increase the levels of afatinib by inhibiting P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Co-administration should be avoided, and the afatinib dose should be reduced if not tolerated. Lopinavir and albuterol both prolong the QTc interval. Co-administration should be avoided. Apalutamide decreases the levels of ritonavir and lopinavir by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration should be avoided. Ritonavir increases the levels of apixaban by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration with strong dual inhibitors of CYP3A4 and P-gp should be avoided. Lopinavir and apomorphine both prolong the QTc interval. Co-administration should be avoided. Lopinavir decreases the levels of apremilast by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. This combination is contraindicated. Ritonavir increases the levels of aprepitant by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration should be avoided. Lopinavir and arformoterol both prolong the QTc interval. Co-administration should be avoided. Lopinavir increases the levels of aripiprazole by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Both drugs prolong the QTc interval. Co-administration should be avoided. Lopinavir and artemether both prolong the QTc interval. Co-administration should be avoided. Lopinavir and asenapine (including transdermal formulations) both prolong the QTc interval. Co-administration should be avoided. Lopinavir increases the levels of atazanavir by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration should be avoided. Ritonavir may interfere with the manufacturing of atidarsagene autotemcel. Antiretroviral therapy should be discontinued for at least one month before cell mobilization. Lopinavir and atomoxetine both prolong the QTc interval. Co-administration should be avoided. Lopinavir increases the levels of atorvastatin by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration should be avoided due to the risk of myopathy. Ritonavir increases the levels of avanafil by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors is contraindicated due to the risk of severe adverse events. Ritonavir and lopinavir increase the levels of avapritinib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors should be avoided. Ritonavir increases the levels of avatrombopag by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration should be avoided. Lopinavir increases the levels of axitinib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. If co-administration with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors is unavoidable, the axitinib dose should be reduced by 50%. Lopinavir increases the levels of bedaquiline by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors for more than 14 consecutive days should be avoided unless the benefits outweigh the risks. Ritonavir may interfere with the manufacturing of betibeglogene autotemcel. Antiretroviral therapy should be discontinued for at least one month before mobilization. Lopinavir increases the levels of bosentan by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration should be avoided. Lopinavir increases the levels of bosutinib by inhibiting P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Co-administration should be avoided.
